items.title: Asian nations rush to buy Russian crude as Iran war chokes oil supply

featured_image.name: Russian oil arrives as Philippines battles 'energy emergency'

items.description:
A growing number of Asian countries are turning to Russia for crude oil as the U.S.-Israeli military conflict with Iran continues to choke off energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, triggering what the International Energy Agency has called the "largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market."[1][2]

The Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, and Sri Lanka have all signaled interest in purchasing Russian crude in recent weeks, joining established buyers China and India in a regional competition for barrels that analysts warn may soon outstrip what Moscow can deliver.[3][4]

items.title: Trump willing to end Iran war without reopening Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: White House: Reopening Strait of Hormuz Not Vital to Ending Iran War

items.description:
President Donald Trump has told aides he is willing to conclude the U.S. military campaign against Iran even if the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed to commercial shipping, The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, a move that could leave Tehran with lasting leverage over one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints.[1]

The shift signals a recalibration of American war aims as the conflict, dubbed Operation Epic Fury, enters its fifth week. In recent discussions, Trump and his advisers concluded that attempting to force the strait open would extend the fighting beyond his preferred four-to-six-week timeline, according to administration officials cited by the Journal. Instead, Washington plans to focus on its stated objectives — degrading Iran's naval and missile capabilities — while pursuing diplomatic channels to persuade Tehran to restore maritime traffic.[1]

items.title: US struck Isfahan ammo depot with bunker busters

featured_image.name: Iran War News: Massive Blasts In Iran's Isfahan After US-Israeli Strikes,  Trump Shares Video

items.description:
The United States struck a large ammunition depot in the Iranian city of Isfahan with a high volume of 2,000-pound penetrator munitions, according to a U.S. official cited by The Wall Street Journal. The strike triggered a chain of secondary explosions that lit up the night sky, with footage of towering fireballs circulating widely after President Trump shared an uncaptioned video of the attack on his Truth Social platform on Sunday evening. The Wall Street Journal confirmed the footage depicted the Isfahan operation.[1][2][3]

The strike is the latest in more than a month of sustained U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran, launched on February 28 under what the Israel Defense Forces have termed "Operation Roaring Lion". Since then, more than 15,000 Iranian targets have been hit, according to the IDF, with the daily strike tempo declining from roughly 1,000 targets in the opening days to fewer than 100.[4][5][6]

items.title: Iran says ambassador will stay in Beirut despite Lebanon's expulsion order

featured_image.name: Iran Says Envoy Will Remain in Beirut Despite Lebanon Order to ...

items.description:
Iran on Monday openly refused to comply with Lebanon's order to expel its ambassador, declaring that the envoy would remain in Beirut and continue his duties — a direct challenge to the Lebanese government's authority that has deepened a diplomatic crisis at the heart of the broader regional conflict between Israel and Hezbollah.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei confirmed at a news conference that Ambassador Mohammad Reza Shibani had no plans to leave. "Our embassy is open and our ambassador continues his work in Beirut and remains present," Baghaei said, according to Iran International. The statement came one day after a March 29 deadline set by Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi for Shibani to depart the country.[1][2][3]

items.title: NYU closes Abu Dhabi campus after Iran threatens US universities
items.description:
New York University has temporarily shut down its Abu Dhabi campus after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared American university outposts in the Middle East "legitimate targets" for retaliation, marking a sharp escalation that extends the ongoing conflict into the realm of civilian academic institutions.

The closure, announced on Monday, suspends physical access to the campus for all students, faculty, and staff, with classes continuing remotely, according to NYU's student newspaper, Washington Square News. The university said the decision was made "out of an abundance of caution" following the IRGC's threat on Sunday.[1][2]

items.title: Kuwaiti oil tanker hit by projectile near Dubai port

featured_image.name: Kuwait says its giant crude oil tanker Al-Salmi was directly targeted by an  Iranian attack while anchored in the anchorage area of Dubai Port, UAE. The  tanker was fully loaded at the

items.description:
A fully loaded Kuwaiti crude oil tanker was struck by a projectile while anchored near Dubai port early on Tuesday, March 31, sparking a fire onboard and raising fears of an oil spill in the Persian Gulf, according to Kuwait's state news agency and a British maritime monitoring authority.

Kuwait Petroleum Corporation said the very large crude carrier Al Salmi was "directly targeted in what it described as an Iranian attack while in the anchorage area of Dubai Port in the United Arab Emirates," the state news agency KUNA reported, as cited by Reuters. The corporation warned of a possible oil spill in surrounding waters, adding that the tanker was fully loaded at the time of the strike. No crew casualties were reported, and emergency response and firefighting teams were mobilized to contain the situation.[1]

items.title: Zelensky says Russia exploiting Iran war to fund its fight against Ukraine

featured_image.name: Russia took satellite images of U.S. air base before Iranian attack ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned Monday that a prolonged war in Iran is delivering outsized benefits to Russia while undermining Ukraine's security, telling Axios in an exclusive interview that Moscow is exploiting the Middle East conflict to boost its war economy and erode Western support for Kyiv.[1]

"I am sure Russia wants long war. They have benefits: The U.S. is focusing on the Middle East and may decrease military help to Ukraine. Sanctions are partially lifted. I see only benefits for Russia from the war with Iran continuing," Zelensky said over Zoom after returning from a tour of Middle Eastern capitals.[1]

items.title: Trump threatens to destroy Iran's energy infrastructure if no deal reached

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Trump's approval hits new 36% low as fuel prices surge amid Iran  war, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds | Reuters

items.description:
President Trump on Monday threatened to "completely obliterate" Iran's electric generating plants, oil wells, and Kharg Island — and possibly its desalination plants — if a peace deal is not reached "shortly" and the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened, dramatically escalating his rhetoric as the war entered its 31st day.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that "The United States of America is in serious discussions with A NEW, AND MORE REASONABLE, REGIME to end our Military Operations in Iran," claiming "great progress" had been made. But he warned that absent a deal, "we will conclude our lovely 'stay' in Iran by blowing up and completely obliterating all of their Electric Generating Plants, Oil Wells and Kharg Island (and possibly all desalinization plants!), which we have purposefully not yet 'touched'".[1][2][3]

items.title: Netanyahu says Iran war is 'beyond the halfway point'

featured_image.name: Netanyahu says Iran's uranium enrichment abilities destroyed

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Monday that the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran has passed its midway mark, with the current focus shifting to securing or removing Iran's remaining stockpile of enriched uranium. The remarks came during an exclusive sit-down interview with Newsmax CEO Chris Ruddy in Jerusalem — Netanyahu's first in-depth interview since the war began on February 28.[1][2]

Netanyahu described the mission as "beyond the halfway point" but declined to put a specific timeline on the conflict's conclusion, saying there is still "a lot more to do". He expressed confidence in the trajectory of the campaign, framing Iran as emerging weaker while the U.S.-Israel alliance grows stronger.[3]
